question: A man goes to Ahmedabad from Kolkata at a speed of 78 km/hr and returns to Kolkata at speed of 91 km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance travelled is the same for two different speeds, the average speed is given by the direct formula: (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Here, the onward speed x = 78 km/hr and return speed y = 91 km/hr.

Average speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ (78 + 91)

Average speed = 14196 ÷ 169

Average speed = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Kolkata to Ahmedabad (v₁) = 78 km/hr

Speed from Ahmedabad to Kolkata (v₂) = 91 km/hr

Let the one-way distance between Kolkata and Ahmedabad be d km.

 
 Kolkata
 
 
 Ahmedabad

 
• 
 
 Distance = d
 
 

 

 Speed 1 = 78 km/hr
 
 

 

 Speed 2 = 91 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance for the round trip = d + d = 2d

⇒ Total Time taken = (Time taken for onward journey) + (Time taken for return journey)

⇒ Total Time = (d ÷ 78) + (d ÷ 91)

⇒ Taking the LCM of 78 and 91, which is 546.

⇒ Total Time = (7d + 6d) ÷ 546

⇒ Total Time = 13d ÷ 546 = d ÷ 42 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 2d ÷ (d ÷ 42)

⇒ Average Speed = 2 × 42 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a journey involves covering 3 equal distances at speeds x, y, and z respectively, the average speed is (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed in the Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction at speeds v₁ and v₂ (where v₁ > v₂), their relative speed is the difference of their speeds: (v₁ − v₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other at speeds v₁ and v₂, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: (v₁ + v₂).
